picks.headline: Guatemala's growing book market debates 'AI and Authorship'
picks.excerpt: Coverage of Guatemala's book market includes a CONTEC Guatemala panel titled 'AI and Authorship' where a literary translator, publisher, and writer debate how translators can leverage AI tools while arguing human translators remain essential because literary translation requires original linguistic solutions tailored to each text.
picks.rationale: Single-topic craft hook on how literary translators can fold AI into their workflow while defending human judgment - actionable for translation/authorship work, and not previously published (distinct from the IPA sessions).

picks.headline: AI narration adoption and LLM book-scanning surface in the week's book-world roundup
picks.excerpt: Weekly roundup touching several AI-and-books threads: an Australian audiobook survey found 17.4% of respondents had tried AI narration/text-to-speech, and reports that U.S. AI firms are buying (and scanning) large quantities of secondhand German-language books to train LLMs.
picks.rationale: Two fresh, distinct AI-and-books data points (a new Australian AI-narration adoption survey and physical-book scanning for LLM training) not in the published history - the audiobook thread is a different survey/geography than the already-published US Spoken/APA study.

picks.headline: AI-accused writer wins a major prize as Google Play Books adds a Gemini reading companion
picks.excerpt: Weekly book-news roundup whose lead items include a writer accused of using AI winning the Commonwealth Short Story Prize and Google Play Books rolling out 'Book Insights,' a Gemini-built reading companion offering recaps and spoiler-free in-book Q&A.
picks.rationale: Distinct outlet with two design-relevant AI hooks - a shipping Google Play Books Gemini reading feature and an AI-in-creative-writing prize controversy - neither of which appears in the 5-day published history.
